OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must contain 8 to 15 digits after
            the '+'. Stored and returned in E.164 form (e.g. '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The owner's 4-digit postcode. Optional; when present it must be
            valid for the owner's city per the fixed city-to-region table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known
            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. An out-of-range postcode is
            rejected with 400. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 4
          maxLength: 4
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The owner's date of birth. Optional; when present it is used to
            derive the read-only 'ageBand', the owner's age band computed
            against the registrationDate. Stored and returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only flag. Owners with the same lastName and postcode belong to
            the same household (they share a deterministic householdId). When such
            an owner already exists a create request is rejected with 409 Conflict;
            setting this flag true bypasses that block, admitting the owner as a
            declared household member (which is not flagged as a possible duplicate).
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32

## What I did

I prepared two seams so the structured-address change can land naturally, without implementing any of it.

**1. Controller — `OwnerRestControllerV1`** (`normalizeNewOwner` / `normalizeAddressFields`)
The address step was inlined inside `normalizeNewOwner`, alongside telephone, email, postcode and registration-date handling. I extracted it into a focused, documented `normalizeAddressFields(Owner)` helper — matching the controller's existing style of small single-purpose helpers (`emailDomainIsBlocked`, `rollToBusinessDay`, etc.). Now `normalizeNewOwner` reads as a sequence of per-concern steps, and the multi-field structured-address logic has one method to grow into rather than swelling the orchestrating method.

**2. Model — `Owner` / `OwnerDerivations`** (address getters/setters)
Flat-address normalization was arithmetic living directly on the `Owner` entity — an anomaly, since every other pure derivation (`region`, `householdId`, `identityKey`, `customerCode`, `ageBand`, …) lives in `OwnerDerivations`, with `Owner` exposing thin delegating methods. I moved the normalization body into `OwnerDerivations.normalizeAddress` and left `Owner.normalizeAddress` as a thin façade delegating to it (mirroring `regionForOwner`, `computeCustomerCode`, `computeHouseholdId`). This establishes the home where the upcoming address-composition and structured-vs-flat fallback derivations will naturally sit, keeping `Owner` lean as it gains the structured `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` fields.

Both changes are pure, behavior-preserving refactors: the controller still normalizes and rejects blank addresses identically, and `Owner.normalizeAddress` returns exactly what it did before. The public API the controller depends on (`Owner.normalizeAddress`) is unchanged.
